This targeting is further linked to Stigmastane-3,6-diol and 6,4'-Dimethyl-Naringenin, both of which are known to interact with P-glycoprotein. These compounds are also known to modulate the activity of the Solute carrier organic anion transporter family member 1B1, suggesting a possible role in the regulation of anion transport across cellular membranes.

Additionally, ursodeoxycholic acid is shown to target Ribosomal protein S6 kinase 2, which is involved in the regulation of protein synthesis and cellular signaling. This kinase is also a target of 6,4'-Dimethyl-Naringenin, which in turn interacts with the Solute carrier organic anion transporter family member 1B1. The presence of multiple independent pathways linking ursodeoxycholic acid to the transporter suggests a complex, multi-tiered mechanism of action that may involve both direct and indirect interactions with the target.

While the evidence is consistent and the pathways are well-documented, the exact nature of the interaction between ursodeoxycholic acid and the Solute carrier organic anion transporter family member 1B1 remains somewhat unclear. The mechanisms by which these compounds modulate the transporter are not fully elucidated, and further experimental validation would be necessary to confirm the biological relevance of these interactions.
